PRP for Interviewers (LMPRPLAN1)
Thursday 3 April from 10am till 12pm in QB4
Description
This module is for managers who are responsible for carrying out the PRP
interviews with staff. Learning Outcomes At the completion of this
seminar managers will be able to
*	confidently prepare for interviews they will carry out with
staff members; and 
*	be able to evaluate and plan workloads and development
opportunities for the forthcoming year. 
Topics
Issues that will be covered in this seminar include
*	Planning 
*	Interviewing 
*	Evaluating 
*	Assessing 

Massey University - The Big Picture (NSINDUCT2)
Friday 4 April from 9:30am till 2pm in Study Centre staff lounge
Description This seminar is targeted towards new staff at the
University, and staff who have not attended the Induction day
previously. Learning Outcomes At the completion of this seminar staff
will have
*	received a formal welcome to the University; 
*	had an opportunity to meet other new staff from across the
University; and 
*	engaged in learning about organisational issues and the wider
Massey University context. 
Topics
Issues that will be covered in this seminar include
*	Team Interviews 
*	A Welcome from the AVC (Academic) 
*	Tertiary structures and procedures 


Knowledge Management in Research 1 (RESKMAN1)
Thursday 3 April from 9:15am till 1pm in CL IIMS5
Description
The focus of this seminar is on knowledge in the emerging electronic
environment. Libraries use computers to find information. University
staff and researchers cannot avoid the use of computers and information
technology in the gathering and storing of information.

Learning Outcomes
On completion of this seminar, you will have

been directed to the location of the best information sources; 
assisted to keep up with the latest research; 
received tips for database searching; and 
received guidance with bibliographic software. 
Topics
Issues that will be covered in this seminar are

Traditional and electronic information environments 
Information and the internet 
Academic authority and information overload 
Database searching 
Knowledge Management 
Bibliographic management software; e.g. Endnote 
Role of life-long learning 


Knowledge Management in Research 3A: Introductory EndNote (RESKMAN3A)
Thursday 3 April from 1:30pm till 4pm in CL IIMS5
Description
To gain credit for RESKMAN3(A+B) staff will need to attend both the
Introductory and Advanced EndNote sessions. The EndNote sessions will be
run in a computer lab environment to enable hands-on practice.

EndNote, a database programme for storing and managing bibliographic
references, is the University's preferred bibliographic management
programme.

EndNote allows staff/researchers to:

create, store and manage references and citations; 
import and store references from electronic databases; 
sort and search references; 
create bibliographies instantly in a variety of bibliographic styles;
and 
insert citations into Microsoft (MS) Word documents. 
Learning Outcomes
On completion of this seminar, you will be able to

create and manage EndNote Libraries; 
insert citations into a MS Word document; 
format a bibliography in MS Word; and 
add records directly to an EndNote Library from bibliographic databases.

Topics
Issues that will be covered in this seminar are

Opening an EndNote Library and creating a new EndNote Library 
Adding records to a Library manually 
Adding database records to an EndNote Library 
Adding database records to an EndNote Library using a filter 
Viewing and selecting a bibliographic style 
Searching for text within a Library 
Sorting records in a library 
Inserting citations into an MS Word document and inserting pagination
details 
Formatting a bibliography within Word 
Backing up your EndNote Library 


Knowledge Management in Research 4: The Scholarly Internet: Google
Scholar and Google Book (RESKMAN4)
Friday 4 April from Thursday 3 April from 9:15am till 1pm in CL IIMS5
Description
Among the new products launched by Google over the past two years are
two that are almost too hot to handle - Google Scholar and Google Books.
Researchers who haven't already tried searching for information through
Google Scholar will probably want to know what it does for them that
conventional databases and ordinary Google searches don't. Those who are
already using it will want to know how to get full value out of their
searches and should also understand its limitations.

Google Books will find search terms from within the text of literally
hundreds of thousands of books, allowing researchers to scan them before
they decide to get hold of a copy. This session will enable attendees to
extend the scope of their document gathering and to save themselves
valuable time through the use of these novel information products.

Learning Outcomes
On completion of this seminar, you will have:

an understanding of Google Scholar: what it is and what it does 
knowledge of how Google Scholar compares with conventional information
sources 
practical hands-on experience searching Google Scholar 
experience of linking information to documents 
an understanding of Google Books: what it is and what it does 
practical hands-on experience searching Google Books 
knowledge of the limitations of Google products 
Topics
Issues that will be covered in this seminar are

Google Scholar: what is it and what does it do? 
Comparison with conventional sources 
Searching Google Scholar 
Linking to other documents 
Google Books: What is it and what does it do? 
Searching Google Books 
Limitations of Google products 



Knowledge Management in Research 3B: Advanced EndNote (RESKMAN3B)
Friday 4 April from 1:30pm till 4pm in CL IIMS5
Description
To gain credit for RESKMAN3(A+B) staff will need to attend both the
Introductory and Advanced EndNote sessions. The EndNote sessions will be
run in a computer lab environment to enable hands-on practice.

EndNote, a database programme for storing and managing bibliographic
references, is the University's preferred bibliographic management
programme.

This session is designed for staff/researchers who have completed the
Introductory EndNote course, and experienced users.

Learning Outcomes
On completion of this seminar, you will be able to

modify reference types, bibliographic styles and filters; 
utilise "Travelling Libraries"; 
add images, PDFs and stored electronic documents to EndNote libraries; 
work with diacritical marks and non-Roman characters; 
Use EndNote as a search engine. 
Topics
Issues that will be covered in this seminar are

Creating and modifying reference types 
Modifying a bibliographic style within EndNote 
Formatting multiple documents to create a single bibliography 
Linking to images, PDFs and stored electronic documents from EndNote
records 
Inserting non-Roman characters 
Using EndNote connections to search library catalogues and open access
databases 
Removing field codes from MS Word documents 
Trouble-shooting and common problems.
